2fa78d4.summary: Per-frame fade of the targeting crosshair sprite and line material alpha, in or out depending on the fade direction flag. When fully faded out, disables the controller, restores the mouse cursor and hides the crosshair and line objects.
comments: Need both the crosshair sprite and the line material; otherwise bail out (null check)
Fade the crosshair sprite alpha: up when fading in, down when fading out, scaled by colorChangeSpeed
Apply the same fade step to the line effect material color
Fading in: stop once alpha has reached 1 (fully visible), nothing more to do
Fading out and alpha reached 0: switch the reticle off completely
Turn off this component, show the normal mouse cursor again, and reset the fade direction
Hide crosshair and line objects, then reset their colors (the SetColor calls apply the cleared color)

2fa7d54.summary: Sets up the targeting reticle: grabs the line renderer's material, hides the crosshair instantly, then builds three planes (floor, player minion row, enemy minion row) from reference transforms for later raycasts. Called once when the reticle is created.
comments: Cache the line renderer material used for fading the targeting line
Start with the reticle hidden (instant toggle off)
No floor reference transform assigned: log an error (set in the scene or via the FloorPositionReference tag)
Build the floor plane: upward normal through the floor reference position
Normalize the up vector (decompiler inlined Vector3.normalized; falls back to zero if tiny)
Player minion plane: normal is forward, passing through the player minion manager's position
Enemy minion plane: same but with the opposite (back) normal, through the enemy minion manager's position

2fa81d4.summary: Moves the crosshair to the world position under the pointer (raycast onto the board) and rebuilds the curved line's points from the origin to that target. Called while the player aims an attack or ability. Decompiler output here is messy; the point loop is real.
comments: Get the crosshair transform (null check), place it at the target position given in UI space
Raycast the UI position through the board camera to a world position and store it as the crosshair spot
Line effect has no curve profile: nothing to draw
Vector from the origin to the reticle position; distance decides how high the arc is
Ratio of distance to the distance at which the arc reaches maximum height, clamped to 0..1
Normalize the direction (zero vector if the points almost coincide)
Loop over the curve points: place each along the straight line plus a height offset from the curve profile
Straight-line position for this point plus an arc height (min..max blended by distance) scaled by the curve profile
Hand the finished point array to the LineRenderer; garbled tail comes from inlined generics and null checks

2fa7b4c.summary: Shows or hides the targeting crosshair and line, either instantly (sets objects active/inactive and resets colors) or with a fade (re-enables the component so Update fades it). Also hides the mouse cursor while the crosshair is shown.
comments: Instant mode: no animation, apply the final state right away
Cursor is visible only when the crosshair is off
Reset sprite and line colors so the next show starts from the base color
Fade mode: ignore the call if the reticle is already in the requested state
Record the new direction, hide or show the cursor, and make sure both objects are active so the fade is visible
Enable the component so Update runs the fade, and log the new fade direction

2fa8420.summary: Starts aiming from a board position: moves the crosshair there, redraws the trail, sets the attack type and color presets, and plays a punch-scale animation on the crosshair sprite. Most of the body is inlined DOTween (DOKill and DOPunchScale) code from the decompiler.
comments: Closure fields saved for the inlined DOTween delegates (target, start position, attack type)
Convert the board position to a 2D world/UI position and move the crosshair root there
Redraw the trail line from the start position
Tell the line effect which attack type this is (affects its look)
Loop through the color presets so the one matching this attack type recolors the sprite and line
Decompiler glitch: the end of the loop was merged with the color-apply code (sets line material color)
If the crosshair sprite is already scaling, kill that running tween first
Inlined DOTween.Kill(transform): scans active tweens targeting this transform; ~300 lines of library internals follow
Inlined DOTween operation switch (complete, kill, pause, play, rewind...); the kill case is the one used
Back in game code: reset the sprite scale to its original size
Start a DOPunchScale tween: a short elastic pulse of the sprite using scaleOnChangeModifier
Unreachable-looking DOTween library code merged in by the decompiler (tween pool cleanup and logging)

2fa84d0.summary: Changes the reticle's attack type: forwards it to the line effect, applies the matching color preset to sprite and line, then kills any running scale tween and plays a fresh punch-scale on the crosshair sprite. Much of the body is inlined DOTween library code.
comments: Let the line effect know the new attack type
Loop over color presets; each one applies its color only if it matches this attack type
Decompiler glitch: loop end merged with the line material color apply
Is the crosshair sprite currently being tweened? If so stop that tween first
Inlined DOTween.Kill(transform): library internals (active tween scan, despawn, logging), not game logic
Back to game code: restore the sprite to its original scale
Start a DOPunchScale on the sprite, strength scaleOnChangeModifier, as visual feedback for the type change

2fa86a4.summary: Immediately hides the crosshair and line effect, shows the mouse cursor again, clears the fade direction and resets the sprite and line colors. Called when targeting ends or is cancelled.
comments: Restore the normal mouse cursor and mark the reticle as fading out
Deactivate crosshair and line effect objects
Reset colors so the next show starts clean

2fa8260.summary: Rebuilds the curved targeting trail between an origin and a target position. If the target is not already in world space it is raycast from UI space to the board first. Writes the arc points to the LineRenderer.
comments: Store the target as the reticle's desired world position
Target given in UI space: raycast it onto the board plane to get a world position
No curve profile on the line effect: nothing to draw
Vector from origin to target; its length sets how high the arc bows
Distance ratio against the max-curve-height distance, clamped to 0..1
Normalize the direction (zero if the points coincide)
Loop over curve points: straight-line position plus arc height from the curve profile
Position along the line plus a height offset blended between min and max height, scaled by the curve
Pass the points to the LineRenderer (decompiler mangled the tail with inlined array helpers)

2fa86b0.summary: Turns a canvas/UI position into a world position on the board: casts a ray through the board camera and intersects it with both the floor plane and the player or enemy minion plane, returning the nearer hit.
comments: Need the battle manager with its HUD and board cameras
Convert the UI position to a screen point, then a ray through the board camera
Intersect the ray with the floor plane; parallel or behind-camera hits count as infinitely far
Pick the minion plane for the chosen side (isPlayer selects the player or enemy row plane)
Same ray-plane intersection against the minion plane
Return the closer of the two hits

2fa8a3c.summary: Auto-aim update: takes the crosshair's current position, raycasts it to world space as the desired target, and rebuilds the curved line from the starting world position to it. Used when the crosshair moves by itself rather than following the mouse.
comments: Take the stored start point of the line
Use the crosshair's own position as the target and raycast it onto the board
No curve profile on the line effect: nothing to draw
Offset from start to target; distance controls the arc height
Ratio to the max-curve-height distance, clamped to 0..1
Normalize the direction (zero vector for near-identical points)
Loop over curve points: straight-line position plus arc height from the curve profile
Point position along the line with the arc height added
Send the points to the line renderer (tail is mangled by inlined helpers)

2fa8a98.summary: Editor-time validation: if the floor reference transform is not assigned, looks it up by the FloorPositionReference tag and logs an error if none exists.
comments: Floor reference missing: find it by tag
Still missing after the lookup: log an error

2fa9414.summary: Static constructor that creates the shared closure-class instance used by AlternateArtStyleIconsSO lambdas.

2fa9484.summary: Predicate used when filtering alternate art style items: true if the item's asset reference is set (non-null).
comments: True when the style item has an asset reference assigned
